# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires the wire colors in the order purple, blue, green. Since I cannot speak and Deaf cannot touch the bomb, I will encode the three color-name lengths as three gesture groups: 6, 4, and 5. Deaf can match those lengths to the visible wire colors and relay the sequence to Blind on the next round.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "👌", "👌", "👌", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile findings: strip has three engraved marks. The first is a six-point floral or star-like mark; the second and third are identical angular three-pronged marks. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 8, 1, 5, 3. Nothing has been entered. I cannot sense the display, light, or wire contents.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, green light, three green strip sections, keypad 8 1 5 3 with nothing entered, and wires purple white blue green red orange. I relayed your gesture sequence to Blind as five thumbs-up, four victory signs, five OK signs.

The manual still requires cutting purple, then blue, then green. Deaf can see the gestures and speak the decoded instruction to Blind, so I will send three separated groups whose lengths are the letters in the color names: purple is 6, blue is 4, and green is 5. Separators make the groups unambiguous.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👋", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "👋", "👌", "👌", "👌", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's visual report, but I cannot perceive your gestures. Please use your manual signal to tell Deaf the exact key to press or wire to cut, and have Deaf state that action to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 6 and blue light; all other visible bomb features are unchanged. I relayed your new gesture sequence to Blind as six thumbs-up, wave, four victory signs, wave, five OK signs.

The manual’s first required action is cutting the purple wire. Deaf can see my signal and can then speak the action to Blind, who can perform it. I will use the established six-thumbs signal for “purple,” without adding other gestures that could confuse the message.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the exact required operation to me now: either press keypad position 1, 2, 3, or 4, or cut wire position 1 through 6. If Deaf has not decoded your gestures, ask Deaf to signal the decoded instruction and then tell me.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 9 and blue light; all other visible bomb features are unchanged. I relayed your six thumbs-up gestures to Blind.

The first manual operation remains cutting the purple wire. Purple is wire position 1 in Deaf’s visible left-to-right list. Deaf must decode my signal and tell Blind to cut wire position 1.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please signal only the required action for the current bomb. Use one through four thumbs-up for press keypad position 1 through 4, or one through six victory signs for cut wire position 1 through 6. Use one wave only between separate parts if needed. Then have Deaf say the decoded action aloud to me.

The required current operation is cutting the purple wire. Deaf’s visible wire order puts purple at position 1, and Blind has specified that one victory sign means cut wire position 1. I will send exactly that signal.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
